p. 1a) Oṃ, salutation to Kālikā.

In this *Śrīmahāguhya*, regarding the *Kālīsvalpaṣoḍhānyāsavidyā*: Ānandabhairava is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Uṣṇik is the meter (*chanda*), the venerable *Mahāguhya Kālīkādeśinī* who bestows success is the power (*śakti*), the deity is the venerable goddess *Mahāprakaṭakālikā*, *Hūṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), and *Saḥ* is the power (*śakti*). The remainder is *kilākaṃ*. The application (*viniyoga*) is for the purification of my body and for attaining firmness in what was previously [established].
With palms joined in reverence.
HĀṂ HĪṂ HŪṂ HAIṂ HAUṂ HAḤ || This is the ritual assignment (nyāsa) of the hands and limbs. Now, the meditation (dhyāna).
Manifest below the trident and skull-bowl, accompanied by Śivā, with hands in the gestures of boon and fearlessness, she is formidable; everything else is to be endowed [with her] as before.
Having meditated thus and worshipped with mental offerings,
one should perform the recitation ten times with palms joined in *añjali*, saying:
"O manifest Goddess Kālikā, bestower of mantra-siddhi!"
"I shall perform the sixfold arts; make my body firm."
Now, the ritual placement (nyāsa): *phreṃ hrīṃ chīṃ strīṃ hūṃ hūṃ saḥ svāhā prakaṭakālikāyai namaḥ svāhā*.
On the base: Oṃ, obeisance to Ghorakālikā, svāhā. On the liṅga:
Oṃ draṃṣṭriṇī kālikāyai namaḥ svāhā. [At] the navel.
Oṃ, obeisance to Ghorakālikā, svāhā! At the heart:
Oṃ, obeisance to Aṭṭāṭṭahāsakālikā, svāhā! At the throat.
Oṃ, homage to Śiromālinī Kālikā, svāhā! [At] the center of the eyebrows.
Homage to Meghaprabhākālikā, svāhā! In the center of the heart.
Oṃ, homage to Kharvakālikā, svāhā! [To be placed] on the forehead.
Oṃ, homage to Kālikā, the bestower of victory; svāhā! [At the mouth.]
Oṃ, obeisance to Sṛṣṭikālikā, svāhā! [This mantra extends] from the base to the left hand.
Oṃ, homage to Sthitikālikā, svāhā! [This extends] from the base up to the right hand.
Oṃ, obeisance to Saṃhārakālikā, svāhā! [This extends] from the Brahma-randhra up to the throat.
Oṃ, obeisance to Bhāsākālikā, svāhā! [This mantra is applied] from the throat to the heart.
Oṃ, homage to Nākṣākālikā, svāhā! [This mantra extends] from the heart to the navel.
Salutation and Svāhā to Kālikā, the essence of the sacred tradition; [this is applied] from the navel to the end of the left side.
Oṃ, homage to Kaurasākālikā, svāhā! [This mantra is applied] from the navel to the end of the right foot.
Oṃ, homage to Kālikā, the essence of the secret; svāhā! [She resides] from the aperture of Brahmā at the crown of the head down to the private parts, extending behind.
Oṃ, obeisance to Kālikā, the essence of the Yoginīs, svāhā. [One should place this] from the ankle to the heel on the back.
Salutation and Svāhā to Kālikā, the essence of all powers.
Hūṃ phaṭ namaḥ svāhā to the glorious, great, manifest Kālikā.
Pervading in three ways from the head to the feet with the syllable *HŪṂ*, one should display the *lelihānā* mudrā and prostrate with palms joined in reverence (*añjali*).
O Goddess who bestows all purity, O manifest one whose form is Brahman!
O Goddess Kālikā, grant me purification of the body; today I worship you.
Thus ends the brief sixfold placement (ṣoḍhānyāsa).
Homage to Śrī Kālikā. Bhairavī said:
O Blessed One, I wish to hear by what cause this is so for a human being.
O Lord, even if recited ten million times, mantras turn away from one who is averse [to the deity].
The illustrious Bhairava said:
I shall tell this secret to you, my beloved.
One should nurture it with great effort, as if it were one's own beloved child.
But one who is diligent in the recitation of the Kālī mantra without the armor-mantra (kavaca) is oppressed.
One does not attain the perfection of meditation even in hundreds of millions of kalpas.
The fivefold armor (kavaca) is to be known: the first is the protector of the body;
the second is named Saṃśupta; the third is Śastabhūṣita.
The fourth is adorned with the power of the seed-syllable and so forth; hear now the fifth, O lady of excellent hips, which has become the mantra that accomplishes all aims upon the earth.

For this armor that protects the body, Kālāgnirudra is the seer (ṛṣi), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chanda), Śrī Mahāguhyakālī is the deity (devatā), Phraṃ is the seed-syllable (bīja), Svāhā is the power (śakti), and the remainder is the pin (kīlaka); its application (viniyoga) is for the protection of my body. Having thus meditated upon the Goddess with joined palms in one's mind, one should recite [the mantra].
PHEṂ: May Kālikā protect my head; may she in her essential form (Svarūpiṇī) protect my forehead and private parts.
May she known as Prakaṭā protect my eyes, and may she known as Vikaṭā protect my ears.
May Draṃṣṭinī protect the two nostrils, and may she of terrible form protect the throat.
Aṭṭāṭṭahāsā is my tongue, and Muṇḍamālinī is my throat.
May Meghaprabhā protect my shoulders, and Kharvakālikā my arms.
May Jayapradā protect the hands, and Caṇḍaghaṇṭikā protect the heart.
May Kuleśvarī protect my chest; may Śaktipriyā, my beloved, protect my hand.
May the matted-haired Yoginī, who moves within the wheel, protect my two flanks.
May Lalajjihvā protect the belly, and Dānavaghāṭinī protect the waist.
May Ghoramukhī protect the navel, and may Jaṭī, the wearer of skins, protect it as well.
She who eats flesh, Śaktinī, she who feeds on semen and blood.
May Khecarī protect my knees, and may Kharparadhāriṇī protect my shanks.
May Kālikā protect my feet everywhere and all my limbs; svāhā!
Thus, O Goddess, I have told you this armor that protects the body.
Without this, success would not be achieved even in hundreds of millions of eons.
It should be given to one who possesses devotion to the guru; it must not be given to just anyone.
To one who is peaceful, pure in thought, devoted to the Goddess, and observant of her conduct—
having recited the armor (*kavaca*), such a person, being composed in mind, should mutter the mantra of the Goddess.
Whether on Mount Urjaṭa, or on a mountain, or even in a cremation ground—whichever one prefers.
O beautiful one, no obstacles whatsoever can arise for him anywhere.
One should completely destroy all preliminary rites and the like by means of the root mantra.

Thus ends the hymn named "The Armor that Protects the Body of the God," which is the secret of Guhyakālī within the *Yoginīhṛdaya*. Now follows the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the wheels (*cakra*). For this ritual placement of the face of all accomplishments (*sarvasiddhi-vaktra-nyāsa*), Bhairava is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (*chandaḥ*), Sarvabhakṣā is the deity (*devatā*), *phreṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), *saḥ* is the power (*śakti*), and the remainder is the peg (*kīlaka*). [This is performed] for the attainment of purity of speech and for the pacification of the fault of falsehood.
The application [of the mantra]. (p. 6a) Thus, with palms joined in reverence (*añjali*).
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa).
*Phreṃ hrīṃ cchrīṃ strīṃ hūṃ phreṃ saḥ svāhā*, *nijamūlatamo guṇādhiṣṭhitamūlavaktrāya svāhā*. Thus, [one offers] to the mouth.
Phreṃ Hrīṃ Cchrīṃ Strīṃ Hūṃ Saḥ Svāhā! Svāhā to the one whose side faces are presided over by his own root quality of rajas!
Mark Ji Chek (Mārkaṇḍeya). Page 6b): On the left side.
PHREṂ HRĪṂ CCHRĪṂ STRĪṂ HŪṂ SAḤ SVĀHĀ! SVĀHĀ to him whose sides and faces are presided over by his own root-mantra and the qualities of the sattvas!
On the right side.
PHREṂ HRĪṂ CCHRĪṂ HŪṂ SAḤ SVĀHĀ | To her who possesses three faces presided over by her own root mantra and the triple qualities (guṇas), HŪṂ PHAṬ NAMAH SVĀHĀ.
Everywhere in the form of a mandala. Thus is the placement of the faces.

Of this *Śrī Guhyakālī Sāvitrī* mantra, Brahmā is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chanda*), the Pure Foundation is the *Sāvitrī*, Kālikā is the deity (*devatā*), *Phreṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), *svāhā* is the power (*śakti*), and the remainder is the peg (*kīlaka*). Its application (*viniyoga*) is for the purification of my sacred thread (*pavitra*).
Thus, with palms joined in reverence.
*Phreṃ*, we meditate upon the manifest Sāvitrī, the remover of obstacles, the Gāyatrī; may Kālī inspire us—*svāhā*.
Thus is the consecration of the sacred thread (*pavitrābhi-mantraṇa*).

Now, the purification of the feet and hands: having washed the feet and hands with "Rahu," having sprinkled them with "Dhri," and having written [the syllable] "Krim" on the palms and soles of the hands and feet, one should consecrate them three times with that same seed-syllable (vīja). Then, having consecrated the water three times with that same seed-syllable, one should sprinkle the body with that water. This is the perfection of the body for the attendant of the *Śmaśānakālī* sādhana.
In this Vidyā of the illustrious Mahākālī, the Ṛṣi is Mahāśmaśāna Bhairava, the metre is Trīṣṭup,

the deity is the illustrious Mahāguhyakālī Kalālī, the seed-syllable (bīja) is *cchraṃ*, the power (śakti) is *cchraḥ*, and the remainder is the pin (kīlaka); its application (viniyoga) is for the sake of my attainment of all perfections.
Having recited this with palms joined in reverence, [place it] upon the head.
Salutation to Śrī Mahāśmaśāna Bhairava.
Salutation to the Triṣṭubh meter in the mouth; salutation to the seed-syllable *cham* at the navel.
At the *mūlādhāra*: *cchaḥ* to Śakti, obeisance. At the feet: *śeṣam* to Kīlaka, obeisance.

From the head down to the feet: "The application (*viniyoga*) is for the sake of all my attainments. Thus is the *tryakṣara* (three-syllable) and other nyāsas. *cchrāṃ* to the two thumbs, *namaḥ*. *cchrīṃ* to the two index fingers, *namaḥ*. *cchruṃ* to the two middle fingers, *namaḥ*.

Cchraiṃ, salutation to both ring fingers. Cchrauṃ, salutation to both index fingers. Cchraḥ, salutation to the palms and backs of the hands. Cchrāṃ, salutation to the heart. Cchrīṃ, svāhā to the head. Cchūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock. Cchraṃ, hūṃ to the armor.
cchrauṃ vauṣaṭ to the three eyes; cchraḥ phaṭ to the weapon—one should meditate [thus].
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the supreme meditation upon Karālī.
She has three faces, with complexions of dark blue, yellow, and clear white, and she possesses the splendor of a jeweled serpent.
Then [one should visualize her] with a large severed head, holding a water-pot and a drinking vessel.
She holds a mudrā, a kusha grass blade, and a trident, and wears a garland of severed heads.
Clad in human skin, dark-complexioned, matted-haired, and restless, she entered the abode of the Nāgas.
With a tongue terrifying to behold.
Embraced by Bhairava, she is adorned with the [same] ornaments and positions as before.
Having meditated thus, one should offer three handfuls of flowers with the root mantra.
Having performed the recitation according to one's capacity, one should offer the recitation and present the sacrificial oblation (bali).
Root mantra: O Śrī Mahāguhyakālī Karālikālike, accept this offering (bali)! Grant me all peace! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Then, with palms joined in reverence, he said: "O Kālikā, O goddess Karālī, O you whose nature is the sound 'kala'! May [my suffering] be pacified."
May this worship, performed according to my ability, bestow all accomplishments.

Of this *Śrī Jvālā Prajvali Mahāśmaśāna Guhya Kālī Mantra*: the seer (*ṛṣi*) is Mahāpralaya Kālāgni Rudra; the meter (*chandaḥ*) is Cilāṭ; the deity (*devatā*) is Mahāśmaśāna Jvālā Guhyakālī; *śrīṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), *hrīṃ* is the power (*śakti*), *klīṃ* is the pin (*kīlaka*), *hūṃ* is the armor (*kavaca*), and *phreṃ* is the principle (*tattva*). [May it serve] my fourfold aims.

For the sake of accomplishing the fruit, perform the recitation: *Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ Hūṃ Phreṃ*. 10 Homage to the two middle fingers. 5 Jvārā, O you who look upon those afflicted by fever! 10 Homage to the two ring fingers.
Salutation to the five great, terrifying, and formidable laughs; salutation to the two little fingers.
Salutation to Vidyujjihvā (Lightning-Tongue), whose tongue is a blazing fire of saliva; salutation to the palms and backs of the hands.
5 Mahākrodhamukhi 10, homage to the heart.
To the one who paralyzes the tongues of enemies, svāhā to the head! || 5 || 10 ||
O beloved consumer of the blood of Daityas and Dānavas, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock!
O Jvālāmukhī, who is intoxicated by drinking honey and gazes upon that [intoxication], hūṃ for the armor!
To the one with a wicked heart, garlanded with flesh, and possessing three eyes, vauṣaṭ! (10)
O fulfiller of the desires of those who contemplate you, O terrifier of all worlds!
O Kālikā, whose feet are worshipped by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, and others; O you who cause fever in the secret place of the great cremation ground! Hūṃ Phaṭ! Namaḥ Svāhā!
Phaṭ to the setting [of the sun]! [The Meditation:]
With a terrible, loud laugh, difficult to behold, and with a fearsome, dreadful tongue.
With two fierce and wicked flames that shatter the heads of enemies.
She was a mass of flames, with a roar difficult to behold, her eyes ablaze with fire.
O Mahāmuṇḍā, O Mahāmālā, O Mahāpreta, O Lalāṭikā!
Mounted upon her left foot, and likewise upon the pair of her feet.
And with his great left foot, he made it tinkle.
He has completely traversed the most terrible [realm] that encompasses the entire universe.
The beauty of her waist-belt and anklets was terrifying, like the sloughed skins of serpents.
The ash, which destroys all sins along with its parasol, is marked upon the forehead with the sign of Tripura.
Adorned with the splendor of a crown of matted locks, she has the crescent moon as her crest-ornament.
Vomiting the most terrible fire of the end of the eon from the caverns of her mouth.
And she releases the hālāhala poison into the ten directions.
To the Daityas, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas who worship your lotus feet.
It bestows the fruits of the four aims of human life upon those beginning with Brahmā and upon men as well.
Enveloped by garlands of flames, the great fire was terrifying.
The great stream of sparks vomited by the firebrand was overflowing with pride and arrogance.
A blazing trident and a great sword, with a wicked edge that terrifies the world.
She who laughs with a loud roar, who is difficult to propitiate, the great skull-bearer, and the most wonderful one.
She who holds the great vessel of nectar for those suffering from fever within her lotus-like hands.
By bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, and others, as well as by yakṣas, gandharvas, and rākṣasas.
She whose lotus-feet are served by clay drums, conchs, kettledrums, and other instruments.
She has a mouth fragrant with honey, she is a consumer of food, and she is a devourer of honey, meat, and other such things.
[She is] one who devours the heads of enemies with the folds [of her body] stained by the blood of fish.
Dark as a dense blue cloud, she is a performer of most cruel deeds.
Māhāmāyā, Mahākālī, Guhyakālī, and Kumārikā.
Her garments cast off, her hair disheveled, with full and towering great breasts.
In the midst of a great cremation ground, crowded with bhūtas, pretas, and other spirits.
The goddess Kālasaṃkarṣiṇī, whose very nature is that of Kālarātri.
I bow down with the yoni-mudrā to the Mother of the worlds, who is manifest before me.
Now, the five-fold offering (pañcopacāra-pūjā).
Hrīṃ Hūṃ Phreṃ! O you with eyes like blazing fire, O you who wear a garland of fragrant flowers, O Guhyakālikā! I offer fragrance. [This is] for the fragrance.

Hrīṃ Hūṃ Phreṃ! O fierce Jvālākālikā, blaze forth, blaze forth! O Guhyakālī, whose body is adorned with a garland of *pārijāta* flowers, [this] flower is saluted; I satisfy you. [This is for] the flower.

Hrīṃ Hūṃ Phreṃ! O you who dwell in the great cremation ground ablaze with the flames of incense, roar twice! O Guhyakālī, whose body is perfumed by the great incense and whose garlands of flames are ignited by sandalwood, agallochum, camphor, musk, yellow orpiment, and other substances—O you who are smeared with divine nectar-paste and are as white as camphor, like the flames of the fire of cosmic dissolution—I offer this incense.
(p. 13a) [This is for] the incense. Hrīṃ Hūṃ Phreṃ! O you adorned with divine nectar-paste, white as camphor, and resembling the flames of the fire of cosmic dissolution...
O Guhyakālī, who dances fearfully within the great temple adorned with lamps, I offer this lamp.

Hrīṃ Hūṃ Phreṃ! O you who consume the divine food offering (naivedya) accompanied by the blazing garland of flames, consisting of lamps, honey, fish, buffalo, goat, great meat (mahāmāṃsa), the flesh of boar, and so forth—devour, devour my enemies!
O Guhyakālikā, I offer this food offering (naivedya). [Of the food offering.]

Hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ! O Caṇḍajvālā, you who blaze in the great cremation ground, O Great Cremation Ground Guhyekāli! Blaze, blaze! Come, come! Dance, dance! Stay, stay! Devour my enemies, devour them! Phreṃ, obeisance to Rati-śakti Kālikā, Svāhā! Phreṃ, [obeisance to] Prīti-śakti! Phreṃ Mvluṃ, [obeisance to] Vāruṇī-śakti!
In the hexagon: *Phreṃ*, obeisance to Amṛtā, svāhā.
Phreṃ, obeisance to the one arisen from nectar, svāhā!
PHREṂ! Homage to the one who showers nectar, svāhā!
Phreṃ, to Amṛtākarṣiṇī, four times.
Phreṃ, obeisance to the one who flows with nectar, svāhā!
Phreṃ, to Amṛtamālinī, four times.
In the square: *phreṃ* to Vāruṇī [four times].
PHREṂ to Ghūrṇā, four times.
Phreṃ! To Āmodārāya!
Phreṃ, to Pramodirāyī, four times.
Obeisance, Svāhā! To the glorious Mahāguhyakālī, Karālī, Parāmṛta, Śakti, and Kālikā; Hūṃ Phaṭ! Namaḥ Svāhā!
Thus concludes the worship with divine water.
Phreṃ Aiṃ Sauḥ Saṃ Saḥ Saḥ Sau Aparānanda abhyantī kuru 2 Namaḥ Svāhā.
Thus is the invocation: *Phreṃ Aiṃ Phreṃ* for the cow-mudrā (*dhenū-mudrā*), and *Phreṃ Mluṃ* for the fish-mudrā (*matsya-mudrā*).
One should consecrate the root [substance] ten times with the mantra.
With that substance and the Gāyatrī mantra, one should sprinkle all objects; [this is done] on the head.
Phre mlauṃ; I satisfy the supreme guru.
In three ways: PHREṂ MHRŌṂ, I satiate the power of the Guru; NAMAH SVĀHĀ.
Threefold; then, in the yantra.
Phreṃ, the root mantra: I offer libations to the glorious Mahāguhyakālī Karālī; obeisance! Svāhā!
In three ways: "I satisfy my own self; obeisance, svāhā"—thus in three ways.
With palms joined in reverence.
The divine nectar of the shore, which is the embrace of supreme bliss.
Therefore, Ānanda, not being satisfied with that, I am propitiating Karālī.
p. 31b) Now, the sacrifice for the consumer.

Having meditated upon the Self as consisting of light, from the base of the spine up to the aperture of Brahma, and having recited the root mantra according to one's capacity, one should offer the recitation.
With palms joined in reverence.
The inner light, the manifest light, the pervasive light, and indeed the light itself—this light, accompanied by the three principles (tritatva), is the secret of all lights, ever-present.
Thus one should recollect the Great Saying.
Now, the invocation: having bound the "tortoise-pitcher" (karaka-cchapikā) and meditated upon [the self] as consisting of light from the root (mūla) up to the aperture of Brahmā (brahma-raṇdha).
vahannāśā pūṭena phreṃ hrīṃ vaṃ svāhā ||
Thus one should desire with the yantra.
Having placed the *tattva-mudrā*, [recite]: *phreṃ hrīṃ strīṃ cchrīṃ hūṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ*.

O Śrīmanmahāguhyakālī Karālī, the life-force (*prāṇa*) of the deity is here; *tryāṃ hrīṃ kroṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ*. O Śrīmanmahāguhyakālī Karālī, the soul (*jīva*) of the deity is established here; *tryāṃ hrīṃ kroṃ yaṃ*.
Raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ. O Śrīmanmahāguhyakālī Karālī, may all the deities—the senses, speech, mind, eyes, ears, nose, and vital breaths—come here and remain happily and for a long time; svāhā! 5.
O Śrīmahāguhyakālī Karālī, come here, come here!
